item.title: U.S. Hunger Leverages Amazon Quick and Spaces for Data‑Driven Food Assistance
item.description:
U.S. Hunger Leverages Amazon Quick and Spaces for Data‑Driven Food Assistance

U.S. Hunger has adopted Amazon Quick and its Spaces capability to bring real‑time data insight to its food‑assistance operations.

🔍 Overview

  • Delivered more than 250 million meals.
  • Historically reached 59 countries, now focused primarily on the United States.
  • Reported ~500 % growth over four years while headcount grew only 15–20 %.
  • President and CEO Rick Whitted spent 30 years in banking before leading the organization.

🛠️ How Quick and Spaces Work

  • Quick extracts data from a SQL Server into its in‑memory engine SPICE via nightly refresh jobs at 2 AM ET.
  • Data originates from Impact Manager, the organization’s proprietary cloud‑based platform, and from the Full Cart program that delivers donor‑funded food to households.
  • Spaces provide a shared workspace where colleagues can store documents, definitions, and analyses for a specific business area.
  • Shared definitions of KPIs ensure everyone agrees on metric meanings.
  • A leadership‑wide KPI document was built over more than a year across NetSuite, Salesforce, Impact Manager, and the payroll system.
  • The technology team and a research data colleague prepare datasets and supply definitions to help the CEO interpret information.

📊 Impact on Operations

  • 17 colleagues across executive leadership, technology, Full Cart, finance, compliance, and support have access to Quick.
  • In Quick, the CEO can comment directly on drafts, regenerate reports with incorporated changes, and refine instructions without moving between Word and chat.
  • Chat serves as the CEO’s primary day‑to‑day AI workspace, while Spaces is the most used capability.
  • Using a Space with Salesforce call reports, the CEO drafts instructions on measures, data sources, and definitions for the technology team.
  • Quick provides a live connection to how leadership thinks through problems, allowing others to pick up where the CEO left off in a financial model or KPI framing without scheduling another meeting.

👥 Leadership & Collaboration

  • The organization first learned about Quick at an AWS Social Entrepreneur Accelerator event led by Kat Esser.
  • CTO Ezekiel Brooks enabled access to core Full Cart datasets for the CEO.
  • Rick Whitted remarked, “The families we serve today, their stories are my story.”
  • He also said, “With all the knowledge and data we have, Space reduces as much noise as possible and narrows my discussion.”
  • The financial Space is shared with the CTO, COO, and finance leadership, granting access to tools and business context behind analyses.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Shared definitions and live data reduce reliance on meetings and manual document handling.
  • The combined Quick + Spaces workflow lets the organization scale its impact efficiently while maintaining data‑driven decision‑making.
  • By grounding financial and operational insight in the real stories of families, U.S. Hunger aligns its rapid growth with its mission.

#AWS #DataAnalytics #NonprofitTech #FoodAssistance

Source: How U.S. Hunger connects leaders and data using Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Integrating Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Denodo for Federated Data Access
item.description:
Integrating Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Denodo for Federated Data Access

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Denodo Platform are being used to build and optimize AI agents capable of accessing distributed enterprise data through a semantic layer.

🧩 How it works

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore hosts the agent, manages inbound authentication, and handles the outbound credentials presented to Denodo. The system operates as follows:

  • Planning: A foundation model on Amazon Bedrock plans and writes queries.
  • Communication: The agent communicates with the semantic layer using VQL, which is Denodo’s SQL dialect.
  • Exposure: The Denodo MCP Server uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to expose governed views to the agent.
  • Reasoning: Joins, metric definitions, and row and column filters are maintained within the semantic layer rather than the prompt.

⚙️ Key details

Denodo implements the semantic layer as a data virtualization platform. This allows the agent to access a source mix that includes both cloud and on-premises data, meaning federation is not bounded by an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC).

Component Function
Denodo Virtual DataPort (VDP) The core query engine where semantic-layer objects live, VQL executes, and access policies evaluate.
Design Studio The browser-based authoring surface for VDP.

Data Federation Example

In a scenario where data is distributed across different engines without foreign keys spanning them or ETL jobs to build them, Denodo plans the federated query at execution time to reconcile the shared identifier (cid):

  • Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL-compatible): Customer profile data.
  • Amazon Redshift: Order history.
  • On-premises PostgreSQL: Rewards program data (rewards_account).

Denodo decides what to push into Aurora and Amazon Redshift, what to fetch from the on-premises cluster, and how to combine results without moving data between sources.

🚀 Availability

Denodo on AWS offers two deployment options:

  • Agora: A fully managed cloud service.
  • Self-managed installation: Deployed on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) or Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS).

#AmazonBedrock #Denodo #DataVirtualization #AIAgents #FederatedQuery

Source: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with Denodo and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Strategy Mosaic powers agentic AI on AWS via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description:
Strategy Mosaic powers agentic AI on AWS via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

The latest walkthrough shows how Strategy Mosaic can serve as a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS, letting a Strands agent hosted on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore query a Customer‑360 (C360) domain across Amazon Redshift and Amazon Aurora without ETL.

🔍 Overview

  • This post is co‑written with Zhili Cheng, Principal Product Manager, George Earle, Director, AI Engineering, and Kyler K, Sales Engineer of Strategy.
  • Mosaic implements a dimensional semantic model – attributes, hierarchies, facts and metrics – composed through Strategy’s metric expression syntax.
  • A single Mosaic definition publishes four native protocols:
    • Model Context Protocol (MCP) for AI agents
    • JDBC/ODBC over Trino for SQL clients
    • XMLA for Power BI and Excel
    • REST for custom applications
  • The walkthrough reuses the C360 pattern introduced in earlier posts that used Stardog and Denodo, but now applies Mosaic’s linked‑model pattern.

🧩 How it works

  • Two Mosaic Models are created – one over Amazon Redshift, one over Amazon Aurora – and linked together.
  • Metric syntax supports:
    • Base metrics (e.g., Purchase Amount = price * quantity)
    • Advanced metrics with named filter objects and level qualifiers
    • Compound metrics that combine other metrics
  • The Strands agent reaches Mosaic through the MCP endpoint; joins, metric definitions, and per‑caller row and column filters reside in Mosaic, not in the prompt.
  • User identity flows from the enterprise identity provider through AgentCore Identity, enabling Row‑Level Security (RLS) and Object‑Level Security (OLS) to be enforced end‑to‑end.
  • Execution can be tuned between live pushdown (leveraging the underlying warehouse) and in‑memory execution for agent traffic.
  • The same governed definitions can be published to Power BI, Tableau, notebooks, and custom apps, and exported in Apache Ossie format for tools outside Mosaic.

⚙️ Key details

Item Details
Semantic layer type Dimensional (attributes, hierarchies, facts, metrics)
Modeling path Mosaic Models (self‑service, AI‑assisted) inherit dimensions, ACLs, RLS from Mosaic Schema
Forms ID form for joins, display form for reading; forms resolve names like “Carolyn Inworth” to the underlying cid
Supported systems Cloud warehouses: Snowflake, Databricks; Operational databases: Amazon RDS, Oracle, SQL Server; Analytical engines: Amazon Athena, Trino, SAP HANA; SaaS sources: Salesforce
Protocols MCP for agents, JDBC/ODBC over Trino for SQL, XMLA for Power BI/Excel, REST for custom apps
Source of truth Strategy One (March 2026) release – Mosaic access through the MCP server is enabled by default

🚀 Availability

  • The walkthrough runs on AWS services: Amazon Redshift Serverless for analytical C360 data, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL as the operational system of record, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore hosting the Strands agent.
  • Deployment uses the native AWS data services; no ETL is required to keep the analytical copy current.
  • The MCP server is available by default in the Strategy One release.

This post continues the series that previously demonstrated semantic layers built with Stardog’s ontology‑based knowledge graph and Denodo’s data‑virtualization platform.

#AIagents #SemanticLayer #AWS #Bedrock #StrategyMosaic

Source: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with Strategy Mosaic and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services Source: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with AtScale and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services

item.title: AI Labs Buying Data from Defunct Startups as New Market Emerges
item.description:
AI Labs Buying Data from Defunct Startups as New Market Emerges

AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models, turning the end‑of‑life ecosystem into a nascent data‑resale market.

🔍 Overview

  • When crypto startup founder Keelan Miskell wound down his company, he sold the code base for about $25,000 and a pending ~$15,000 for workspace data (Google, Notion, Figma, Slack) through SimpleClosure.
  • SimpleClosure added data sales to its services in April and now runs an Asset Hub platform that lets founders sell code and workspace data such as emails, chats, and documents.
  • Buyers include foundation AI labs, vendors that build simulated workspaces for AI training, and mature tech companies building their own models.

🧩 How the Market Works

  • SimpleClosure brokered over 150 deals and expects to return > $10 million to startups by the end of 2026.
  • 47 % of SimpleClosure’s deals now include code or data sales, according to CEO Dori Yona.
  • Rival Sunset also runs a data‑resale business; its CEO Brendan Mahony values assets by head count, years in operation, data volume, and tool usage, likening the exhaust data to “particle board.”
  • Demand surged last year as AI labs hit limits of public and synthetic datasets.
  • Companies like Surge AI buy archives to build reinforcement‑learning gyms where agents practice tasks (e.g., debugging IT architecture, drafting appellate briefs). Lead Nick Heiner says a rich Slack history can be more valuable than a combination of Slack, email, and calendars.

📊 Key Statistics

Metric Figure
Annual rise in startup shutdowns 26 %–56 % (Carta & AngelList)
Deals that include code/data (SimpleClosure) 47 %
Asset Hub deals handled >150
Expected return to startups (2026) > $10 M

🤝 Notable Deals & Players

  • Google outbid Mercor for Spirit Airlines’ bankruptcy data: 100 M emails, 500 M Teams messages, 176 k employee records for $10 M (August).
  • SpaceX AI unit is reportedly weighing data purchases from struggling startups (September, Bloomberg).
  • Surge AI purchases real‑world archives to avoid synthetic‑world errors; pricing varies because valuations are based on research theses about task usefulness.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Attorneys like Greg Ewing call the data “legally radioactive,” noting that even after scrubbing, private details (doctor appointments, school pickups, date‑night plans) can remain.
  • Proceeds typically flow to senior creditors and investors, not to employees.
  • Law professor Ifeoma Ajunwa describes the practice as “captured capital” and argues that employers should obtain explicit consent before selling workers’ data, though no federal law currently bans such sales.
  • Founders have little visibility into who purchases their data or how it will be used.

The emerging ecosystem—coaches, “death doulas,” legal and tax specialists—reflects a growing market for the operational exhaust of companies that are winding down.

#AIData #StartupClosure #MachineLearning #DataPrivacy

Source: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models

item.title: Atomic Agent Adds Snowflake Integration via Composio and MCP
item.description:
Atomic Agent Adds Snowflake Integration via Composio and MCP

Atomic Agent, the open‑source on‑device AI assistant, now supports direct interaction with Snowflake through the Composio integration and the Snowflake Model Context Protocol (MCP).

🔍 Overview

  • Atomic Agent runs on your machine and supports local models via llama.cpp.
  • Through Composio it can connect to 1,500+ apps, including Snowflake.
  • Users can issue natural‑language requests such as “list today’s new users” or “cancel a long‑running data import”; authentication is handled automatically.

🧩 How it works

  • Atomic Agent connects to Composio’s Tool Router over Streamable HTTP MCP.
  • For each request the agent discovers the appropriate tools; Composio supplies the necessary account authentication.
  • Execution and account‑connection tools obey the agent’s configured approval policy – you must review any approval prompt before the action proceeds.

⚙️ Setup & Usage

  • Requirements: Atomic Agent v0.5.6 or later, a Composio API key, and a Snowflake account.
  • Add the line below to ~/.atomic‑agent/.env, replacing the placeholder with your key, then start Atomic Agent: 
    1

    COMPOSIO_API_KEY=YOUR_COMPOSIO_API_KEY
  • In Atomic Agent, open the Integrations tab, select Composio, press e, paste the API key, and press Enter. The tools become available immediately, without a restart.
  • Ask Atomic Agent to perform an action in Snowflake. The agent searches Composio for the correct tool. On first use, a sign‑in link is returned in the chat – follow it to connect your Snowflake account, then return to Atomic Agent to continue.

🚀 Availability

  • The Hobby plan includes 100,000 tool calls per month.
  • Integration can be disabled by setting "composio": { "enabled": false } in the config; the saved key remains on disk.

📋 Tool Reference

Tool What it does
Cancel Statement Execution Cancels the execution of a running SQL statement

The Snowflake MCP server implements the Model Context Protocol, giving the agent structured and secure access to the data warehouse and service status. It enables the agent to execute SQL, explore databases and tables, track or cancel statements, inspect catalog integrations, and monitor incidents and maintenance on your behalf.

#AtomicAgent #Snowflake #Composio #AIAgents #MCP

Source: Snowflake MCP Integration with Atomic Agent | Composio

item.title: Veeam Releases Recovery Orchestrator v13.1 with Hyper-V and Azure Support
item.description:
Veeam Releases Recovery Orchestrator v13.1 with Hyper-V and Azure Support

Veeam has launched Veeam Recovery Orchestrator v13.1 as part of the Veeam Data Platform Premium Edition. This release introduces quality-of-life improvements designed to make data orchestration simpler and more flexible, featuring new stand-alone host support, direct-to-cloud restoration, and read-only repository access.

🖥️ Stand-Alone Hyper-V and Cross-Platform Recovery

Orchestrator v13.1 introduces support for a stand-alone Hyper-V host as a recovery target, accommodating both local and shared storage. This update also introduces new migration and recovery pathways:

  • Cross-Platform Restores: vSphere environments can perform cross-platform restores from vSphere VM backups to a stand-alone Hyper-V host. This enables organizations to utilize a lower-cost Hyper-V disaster recovery site to pilot potential platform migrations on a single host.
  • Direct Azure Restores: Hyper-V VM backups can now be restored directly to Azure, joining existing support for vSphere VM and Veeam Agent backups. This feature also supports script injection to the restored virtual machines.

🛡️ Read-Only Repositories and Cleanroom Protection

Building on Veeam Backup & Replication v13.1 features, object storage repositories can now connect to Orchestrator’s embedded Veeam backup server in read-only mode. This configuration provides several key advantages:

  • Continuous Access: Users maintain constant access to the latest restore points, including imported backups, to test recovery plans.
  • Cleanroom Security: Read-only access allows cleanroom recovery environments to pull current data without creating a pathway back to production.
  • Automatic Handoffs: If the production Veeam Backup & Replication server goes down, the embedded backup server can take over failover. This update keeps the data behind that handoff current automatically, eliminating the need for manual connection refreshes.

📍 Upgraded Recovery Locations

Recovery locations have received two key upgrades designed to improve precision without sacrificing automation:

  • Specific Targeting: While automatic selection remains available, users can now target recovery directly to a specific Veeam backup server and the specific repositories it manages.
  • Map From Any Source Network: This catch-all network mapping configuration option allows recovery locations to recover VMs from source networks that have not been explicitly mapped, preventing recovery processes from failing when an unexpected network is encountered.

⚙️ Simplified Day 2 Operations

Day 2 operations and maintenance tasks have been streamlined through a unified installer, a new Scheduled Tasks page, and the new Veeam Updater plug-in, which can be launched directly from the About page in the Orchestrator web UI.

Feature Capability
Update Scheduling & Automation Allows users to define maintenance windows and control when updates are installed.
Mandatory Updates Enforces required patch levels across all managed Veeam Backup & Replication components.
Bulk Update Management Allows users to update multiple infrastructure components simultaneously to streamline maintenance.

#Veeam #DisasterRecovery #HyperV #CloudBackup #DataProtection

Source: What’s New in Veeam Recovery Orchestrator v13.1

item.title: NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit Adds Amazon S3 Vectors for Persistent Agent Memory
item.description:
NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit Adds Amazon S3 Vectors for Persistent Agent Memory

NVIDIA’s open‑source NeMo Agent Toolkit (NAT) now integrates Amazon S3 Vectors as a persistent memory backend, allowing agents deployed on Amazon EKS to store and retrieve long‑term knowledge with elastic scale.

🔍 Overview

  • Open‑source framework for building, profiling, and optimizing AI agents.
  • Framework‑agnostic; works with Strands Agents, LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, and custom implementations.
  • Four core capabilities: Agent orchestration, Profiling, Evaluation, Optimization.
  • Agents are defined as composable workflows with configurable LLMs, tools, and prompts.
  • Execution options: nat run locally or nat serve as a persistent service.

🧩 How it works

  • Includes a dedicated memory subsystem that stores conversation history, user preferences, and long‑term knowledge.
  • Memory module is extensible via a plugin interface; custom providers implement the MemoryEditor abstract interface (add_items(), search(), remove_items()).
  • MemoryItem model holds conversation history, tags, metadata, user_id, and an optional textual memory string.
  • Provider discovery uses the _type field in a YAML configuration.
  • The auto_memory_agent workflow automatically captures and retrieves memory without explicit LLM calls.
  • Amazon S3 Vectors serves as a memory backend: vectors are 1024‑dimensional embeddings generated by Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2, stored with scoped metadata, and searchable with semantic similarity.

⚙️ Key details

Provider Note
Mem0 Built‑in memory provider
MemMachine Built‑in memory provider
Redis Built‑in memory provider
Zep Built‑in memory provider
  • Semantic retrieval with configurable distance metrics (cosine, euclidean).
  • Filterable metadata (strings, numbers, Booleans, lists) on each vector.
  • Memories become visible immediately after insertion.
  • Scale to 2 billion vectors per index with no capacity planning.
  • Pay‑as‑you‑go pricing; no idle compute costs.
  • IAM policies per bucket and index; per‑tenant indexes provide hard isolation.

🚀 Deployment

  • Deployed on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) for full operational control.
  • Requires Python 3.11 or 3.12; NAT version 1.6 tested.
  • Memory plugin integrates Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 (1024 dimensions) and translates search filters into S3 Vectors metadata queries.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides persistent, scalable memory for multi‑agent workflows.
  • Enables detailed profiling of token usage, latency, throughput, and runtimes.
  • Supports automated hyper‑parameter tuning to balance quality, cost, and latency.
  • Leverages AWS’s elastic storage and security model for isolated, cost‑effective deployments.

#NVIDIA #NeMo #AWS #AIAgents

Source: Build agent memory with NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit and Amazon S3 Vectors | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Scaling Machine Learning Workloads with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod and Cloud Data Fabric
item.description:
Scaling Machine Learning Workloads with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod and Cloud Data Fabric

Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers infrastructure for large-scale machine learning workloads on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS). By integrating with Cloud Native Qumulo (CNQ) and Qumulo’s Cloud Data Fabric (CDF), developers can now run training compute in one AWS Region while accessing datasets stored in another without the need to copy data or modify existing code.

🧩 How it works

Cloud Data Fabric maintains a single authoritative copy of a dataset on a hub cluster and projects it to spoke clusters as a unified POSIX namespace. Through predictive caching via NeuralCache, the system learns data loader access patterns and serves data from local NVMe storage. After an initial warmup period, this architecture allows spoke clusters to achieve throughput performance equivalent to locally co-located clusters, even across high-latency network links.

⚙️ Key details

  • Resiliency: The infrastructure continuously monitors node health and automatically replaces faulty nodes to prevent hardware failures from impacting the entire cluster.
  • Performance: Training jobs using this setup reach 98–100 percent GPU utilization after a brief warmup of 100–150 batches.
  • Integration: The solution supports remote job submission via the sagemaker_ray:// protocol and provides pre-built Amazon Managed Grafana dashboards through the HyperPod Observability EKS add-on.
  • Training Frameworks: The platform supports frameworks such as SkyRL, enabling advanced techniques like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for tasks like vision-language model navigation.

📊 Performance Comparison

Cluster Configuration Throughput (samples/sec) Training Time
Hub (Local) 116–117 18.5 minutes
Spoke (Warm Cache) 115–116 18.5 minutes
Spoke (Cold Start) 95–116 ~19–20 minutes

#MachineLearning #AmazonSageMaker #CloudComputing #DataEngineering

Source: Accelerate multimodal RL training with SkyRL on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod | Amazon Web Services Source: Multi-Region training with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod and Qumulo | Amazon Web Services

item.title: End-to-End Framework Automates Business Semantic Layer Construction from Raw Logs
item.description:
End-to-End Framework Automates Business Semantic Layer Construction from Raw Logs

Researchers have introduced an end-to-end framework that fully automates the construction of a business semantic layer from raw application logs, eliminating the need for labeled training data or manual rule engineering.

💡 Why it matters

Modern applications generate massive volumes of raw telemetry data, but translating these noisy, heterogeneous event streams into actionable business insights is a fundamental challenge. Previously, data engineers and analysts spent substantial effort on:

  • Reconciling semantic discrepancies
  • Hand-crafting parsing logics
  • Maintaining fragile mappings between raw data and business KPIs

🧩 How it works

The system utilizes a two-stage semantic abstraction process:

Stage Process
First Stage High-level business features are identified via LLM inference augmented with domain-specific industry knowledge
Second Stage Fine-grained business nodes are derived through a structured pipeline including data refinement, hybrid retrieval, multi-stage filtering, semantic clustering, and canonical naming

⚙️ Key details

Evaluation on production-scale telemetry indicates the following results:

  • Semantic Quality: Human-assessed quality improved from 50 to 80+ on a 100-point scale
  • Efficiency: Maintenance effort was reduced by 80%
  • Noise Reduction: 74% of noise was filtered out
  • Quality Assurance: Achieved 0.87 Cohen’s kappa via an integrated LLM-as-Judge evaluation

#LLM #Telemetry #DataEngineering #SemanticLayer

Source: Semantic Layer Induction from Raw Telemetry via Hierarchical LLM and RAG Abstraction

item.title: New Evaluation Semantics Profile for Croissant ML Dataset Descriptors
item.description:
New Evaluation Semantics Profile for Croissant ML Dataset Descriptors

A new additive profile has been developed to provide evaluation semantics for Croissant, the de facto machine-readable descriptor for ML datasets.

🔍 Overview

While Croissant version 1.1 carries data use conditions—recommending ODRL and DUO—it does not specify how these are evaluated. It lacks a decision procedure, bounds on evaluation cost, outcomes for conditions an implementation cannot evaluate, records of what was checked, and information on composition with caller-side authority.

🧩 How it works

An additive profile allows a dataset to declare admitted operations and the conditions for those admissions. Key technical features include:

  • Closed Operator Set: Uses a closed set of five operators with a full decision procedure.
  • Automated Gating: A gate can decide based on the descriptor alone and record the checks performed.
  • State Space Separation: Caller-bound and data-bound policies range over non-overlapping state spaces, meaning neither permit set contains the other.

⚙️ Key details

Testing was conducted using two corpora with evidence kept apart, as well as a corpus generated from the profile’s grammar to cover every conformance clause, refusal class, and operator.

Deployment Results (nf-core pipeline)

Metric Result
Decision Accuracy Profile document decisions match the gate’s native descriptor record for record
Compatibility Stripping the layer leaves a valid Croissant document
Performance Cost 11.7 $\mu$s added cost against a 119 $\mu$s decision

Additionally, across valid cases, 552 complete decision records showed agreement between the native descriptor, profile terms, and the ODRL policy in usageInfo.

#Croissant #MLdatasets #DataGovernance #ODRL

Source: A Policy Profile for Croissant: Refusal as a Property of the Dataset

item.title: Memanto Introduces Memory Agent for Cross-Platform Agent Memory Management
item.description:
Memanto Introduces Memory Agent for Cross-Platform Agent Memory Management

Memanto has launched a Memory Agent designed to manage the memories of other agents, handling curation, conflict resolution, and expiration across different platforms.

🔍 Overview

While platforms such as Claude, Bedrock, Cursor, and various vector stores provide storage persistence, they do not manage the content of that memory. Memanto acts as a “chief of staff” for an agent fleet, ensuring agents do not hold contradictory beliefs or redo completed work.

🧩 How it works

Memanto is a second agent that runs alongside an existing fleet based on its own judgment rather than acting as a library. It operates via a daily loop enabled by memanto schedule enable to perform the following tasks:

  • Curating new memories
  • Merging duplicates across agents
  • Flagging contradictions for review
  • Resolving contradictions
  • Discarding stale data
  • Briefing agents before they act

⚙️ Key details

  • Integration: Requires no code changes, wrappers, or rewrites of the agent loop.
  • OS Support: Compatible with macOS, Linux, and Windows.
  • Management: memanto ui provides a local dashboard to browse, search, and audit the estate.
  • Data Portability: The estate is stored as a file. Users can use memanto memory export --okf to export data in Open Knowledge Format (plain Markdown).

🚀 Availability

Memanto includes a memanto migrate command for importing and exporting data between the following services:

Service
Mem0
Letta
Supermemory
Any OKF bundle

💡 Why it matters

Memanto addresses the gap between storage and management. It prevents scenarios where a preference from March outranks a decision from last week or where two agents believe opposite things about a service.

#Memanto #AIAgents #MemoryManagement #OpenKnowledgeFormat

Source: moorcheh-ai/memanto

item.title: Automating Custom Permissions Assignment in Quick
item.description:
Automating Custom Permissions Assignment in Quick

Quick has introduced architectural patterns to automate the assignment of custom permissions, allowing organizations to enforce fine-grained access control across the user lifecycle.

🔍 Overview

Custom permissions enable administrators to toggle specific features on or off for individual users. This allows for precise control, such as enabling financial analysts to author reports without exporting raw data, or allowing external partners to view dashboards without accessing sharing controls.

Permissions follow a three-level hierarchy where settings are applied as follows:

  • User-level: Overrides role-level settings.
  • Role-level: Overrides account-level settings.
  • Account-level: The base level of the hierarchy.

🧩 How it works

Organizations can use four architectural patterns to automate permissions based on their specific needs:

Method Application Scenario
RegisterUser API Applies permissions during user creation via the --custom-permissions-name parameter; common for SaaS companies restricting features like GenBI and paginated reports based on pricing tiers.
UpdateAccountCustomPermission API Sets a fallback profile for any user without an explicit assignment, including those created via Just-In-Time provisioning.
UpdateRoleCustomPermission API Sets a default custom permission profile per Quick role (READER, AUTHOR, ADMIN, and PRO roles).
Event-Driven Automation Uses Amazon EventBridge and AWS Lambda to detect new group memberships (native Quick groups or AWS IAM Identity Center groups) and apply permissions dynamically.

⚙️ Key details

  • Conditional Logic: For requirements beyond native defaults—such as applying different profiles based on group membership—event-driven automation is used. This is necessary because there is no native API for assigning custom permissions directly to a Group.
  • Complementary Strategies: Role and account-level defaults (Scenario 2) and group-based automation (Scenario 3) are complementary rather than alternatives.
  • Provisioning Gaps: Because Just-In-Time federation creates a window between account creation and group assignment, Scenario 3 only triggers upon the group membership event.
  • Enterprise Scale: Account-level defaults allow large enterprises to instantly block new features, such as GenBI or connectors, for all users during security reviews without per-user automation.

#Quick #AWS #AccessControl #Automation #IAM

Source: Automate user-level custom permissions for Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store introduces UpdateRecord API for feature-level writes
item.description:
Amazon SageMaker Feature Store introduces UpdateRecord API for feature-level writes

Amazon SageMaker Feature Store has introduced the UpdateRecord API, allowing users to update specific feature values without reading or rewriting entire records.

🔍 Overview

Amazon SageMaker Feature Store is a fully managed repository used to store, share, and manage machine learning (ML) features, which are the processed data used for generating predictions and training models. Features are organized into Feature Groups, which are logical collections of related features used by one or more ML models.

💡 Why it matters

Until now, updating a single feature value within a feature group required a full read-modify-write cycle using PutRecord. The UpdateRecord API removes this cycle, as the client application only needs to call the API with the changed features. Features not included in the request are preserved as-is.

🧩 How it works

The Feature Store service performs the following steps during an UpdateRecord call:

  • Validates AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions.
  • Checks EventTime ordering to reject stale writes.
  • Performs an atomic merge of the provided features.

To ensure training datasets remain accurate, a full record snapshot is automatically replicated to the offline store.

⚙️ Key details

The UpdateRecord API requires the following parameters:

Parameter Description
FeatureGroupName The target feature group
RecordIdentifierValueAsString The primary key of the record to update
Features A list of one or more feature values to set (up to 100 per call)
EventTime Must be newer than the existing stored EventTime or the call is rejected with an HTTP 409 error
TtlDuration (optional) Override or set a per-record time-to-live (TTL)

Note: UpdateRecord is not an upsert; the record must already exist.

🚀 Availability

This capability is available for both online store tiers:

  • In-Memory Tier (Amazon ElastiCache-backed): Feature-level writes work on all existing In-Memory feature groups out of the box.
  • Standard Tier (Amazon DynamoDB-backed): Requires a new storage format named Standard_V2 to support feature-level writes.

Users of the Standard Tier can transition to Standard_V2 by:

  1. Using the Feature Processor SDK to read records from an existing Standard feature group and re-ingesting them into a new Standard_V2 feature group.
  2. Calling UpdateFeatureGroup with OnlineStoreConfig.StorageType = “Standard_V2” to flip the format in place. Once declared as Standard_V2, calls to PutRecord or BatchWriteRecord will update the underlying format to Standard_V2.
